title: The month onion prices fell across India
summary: In May 2007, the median onion market moved -18.2% in a month, 2.4 standard deviations from the usual for that month.
why_selected: Chosen automatically: the 2.4σ seasonal move is among the largest on record for onion, across 298 reporting markets.

evidence.observations: monthly medians of daily modal prices; markets need ≥5 reports in both months
caveats: Many market points are district centres, not mandi gates.
Modal prices are reported aggregates, not transaction offers.

scenes.headline: May 2007
scenes.caption: Onion prices across 298 markets that reported in both April 2007 and May 2007.

scenes.headline: Median move -18.2%
scenes.caption: The typical market's onion price fell 18.2% in one month. 90% of markets moved the same way.

scenes.headline: 2.4× the usual swing
scenes.caption: Compared with the same month in every earlier year on record, this move was 2.4 standard deviations from normal.

scenes.headline: Haryana
scenes.caption: Neighbouring markets moved together: the 28 reporting markets in Haryana had a median change of -27.9%.

scenes.headline: Fatehabad
scenes.caption: Fatehabad (Haryana), one of the busiest markets among the biggest movers: monthly median ₹700 → ₹400 per quintal (-42.9%).

scenes.headline: What this does and doesn't show
scenes.caption: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.

conclusion: These are reported wholesale modal prices, not causes. Weather, arrivals or policy may explain the move, but this story shows only what markets reported.
